correctness.rationale: The published criterion reduces all \(m\ge3,d>m\) cases and all \(m=2,d\ge4\) cases to positive closed-form binomial differences; the published boundary and low-dimensional theorems cover the remaining already-settled cases. For the sole new case \((m,d)=(2,3)\), the proof stratifies possible second cones by the gcd degree \(s\) of their restrictions to \(K=H\cap H'\). For \(n\ge4\), the restriction of a general cone quadric has rank at least \(4\), so \(s\in\{0,2\}\). The published two-cone Hilbert functions give fixed-cone codimensions \(D_n(2)+2n-2\) and \(D_n(2)\). The \(s=0\) stratum is too small, while the two \(s=2\) subfamilies have dimensions at most \(2n-1\) and \(4n-4\), both below \(D_n(2)\). The same-support case is excluded by irreducibility of the general quadric and \(B(p)\ne0\). Hence a general cubic in \(L_C\) has a unique cone.

value.rationale: The result completely resolves an explicit open problem in a new algebraic-geometry paper. It upgrades a sufficient higher-dimensional criterion to an exact all-parameter statement and isolates the sole non-birational family, whose generic degree is already known exactly. Birationality is the condition that turns the paper's incidence Segre integral into the degree of the image without an unknown generic-degree factor, so the result has direct enumerative meaning rather than being a routine boundary calculation.
